cluster_summary: This cluster contains five distinct vulnerabilities where sensitive data—such as authentication tokens, private keys, credentials in URLs, and deployment details—are exposed due to missing or incomplete redaction, authorization checks, or secret isolation. Each vulnerability arises from a different coding oversight but all lead to information disclosure.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs into the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs. Report code paths where the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 1 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should Introduce a dedicated secret resolution function that only uses the intended configuration secret and never falls back to authentication tokens; auto-generate a new secret if missing..

sub_patterns.root_cause: The code assumed that any available secret (gateway auth token) could be reused as a hashing secret for owner display obfuscation without considering cross-domain security implications; no isolation of cryptographic secrets per use case.
